meta.name: A Warming World, Year by Year
meta.description: NASA's map of global surface temperature, one year per second from 1880 to 2025, with instruments: the year's figure as a counter, the record as a line that grows in step, and stops at the years that stand out. Start in the decade you were born.
meta.creator: demo

body.frametrail:name: The record as a line
body.frametrail:licenseAttribution: Drawn for this example from NASA's GISTEMP v4 table

frametrail:attributes.text: <p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>The coldest year</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">1909 is the coldest year in the record: −0.48 °C.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>A wartime peak</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">A warm spell peaks at +0.20 °C. Measurements at sea are less certain than usual in these years.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>The last cool year</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">1976 is the last year below the 1951–1980 average. Every year since has been warmer.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>El Niño</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">A strong El Niño lifts 1998 to +0.61 °C, well above the years around it.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>One degree</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">2016 is the first year a full degree above the average: +1.01 °C.</span></p>
<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>The warmest year</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 14px;">2024 is the warmest year in the record so far: +1.28 °C.</span></p>

<p><span style="font-size: 19px;"><strong>2025: +1.19 °C</strong></span></p><p><span style="font-size: 13px;">Map: NASA Scientific Visualization Studio. Figures: NASA GISTEMP v4, annual means.</span></p>
